input.evidence_text: Hindley couple spent 20 years building railway station garden - BBC News Image caption, The community garden has been created beside both platforms at Hindley station in Wigan By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago A couple who have spent 20 years building a community garden at their local railway station have said they hope it will be named as the Best in Britain. Hindley Station in Wigan has been nominated in an annual "World Cup" of stations competition run by train operating companies. Sheila and Sandy Davidson have been planting trees, flowers and shrubs alongside the platforms for two decades. "We just came down almost 20 years ago and decided to plant a few bulbs on the Manchester-bound platform," said 80-year-old Sheila from the Friends of Hindley Station. "Everybody in the area is wonderful, they all support us and we get so much help from people on social media who donate things for the garden." Image caption, Sheila Davidson is the Friends of Hindley Station's lead volunteer Sheila added: "It's putting Hindley on the map, so to even get in the World Cup of stations is such an honour, but we really would like to win." The Rail Delivery Group, which represents train operating companies, organises the competition every year, with passengers voting for the winner. Ashington railway station in Northumberland won the award last year after passenger services returned to the town in 2024 following an absence of 60 years. Image caption, The platforms at Hindley Station have been turned into vibrant community gardens and allotments Hindley station opened in 1848 and is situated between Bolton and Wigan, with regular direct services across the north of England. title: Historic pub objects to plan for 17-storey tower nearby

input.lead: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.summary: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.evidence_text: Historic pub objects to plan for 17-storey tower nearby - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 17 October 2026 A historic Manchester pub that has drawn visitors from around the world is fearing for its future amid plans for a large tower to be built nearby. The Marble Arch has been serving pints on Rochdale Road since 1888 when Queen Victoria sat on the throne and the city was rapidly industrialising. Plans by the McGoff Group to build a 17-storey tower with 153 flats next to the Grade II-listed pub have prompted concerns about the visual impact and the pub's continued existence. Manchester City Council said it accepted "some visual harm" would be caused as a result of the building going up, but would be "outweighed by the substantial public and regeneration benefits that the proposal would deliver". Councillors in Manchester have been recommended to approve the plans at a meeting on 22 October. The McGoff Group has been approached for a comment. Meanwhile, the Marble Arch has submitted a detailed objection against the plans, alongside the Victorian Society and Campaign for Real Ale. One member of staff at the pub told the Local Democracy Reporting Service that the pub is in a "battle" for its future. They said it had already endured "years" of major roadworks. "We get tourists coming from all over the world and they get sent here," they said. "These plans are going to be really tough, but we're fighting it and doing everything we can. "We have generations of families drinking here, dads and granddads and sons. You don't get places like this anymore and it's something we want to keep going." Image source, Stephen McKay/Geog

title: Rochdale school with over 1,000 pupils evacuated over hoax bomb threat

input.lead: Police say a bomb threat which was called into St Cuthbert's Roman Catholic High School was a "hoax"
input.summary: Police say a bomb threat which was called into St Cuthbert's Roman Catholic High School was a "hoax"
input.evidence_text: Rochdale school with over 1,000 pupils evacuated over hoax bomb threat - BBC News Image caption, St Cuthbert's Roman Catholic High School was put into lockdown by school staff after the bomb threat By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 16 October 2026 A school of more than 1,000 pupils was evacuated after a hoax bomb threat was made. St Cuthbert's Roman Catholic High School was put into lockdown after the bomb call at 08:55 BST and staff dialled 999. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it investigated but found it was a hoax. The school, which has more than 1,100 pupils, has been closed for the day. GMP said it was investigating. A GMP spokesman said: "The school implemented a lockdown in response to a suspicious call. "Officers attended and carried out an assessment which indicated that the call was a likely hoax. "Officers are investigating the circumstances of the call." The trust which runs the school, St Teresa of Calcutta Catholic Academy Trust, said "parents and carers were notified immediately that their children had been removed to a safe distance and there was no threat or danger to anyone present". 'False rumours' A statement on Facebook added: "We would like to assure everyone within the St Cuthbert's School community that the safety and wellbeing of our children remains our absolute priority." The trust urged people to "avoid speculation on social media - particularly regarding false rumours, such as any referring to intruders or weapons being present on school premises". It added: "The current expectation is that the school will be open as normal on Monday 19 October and further details will be shared when appropriate." Earlier this year, staff at St Cuthbert's held a series of strikes over claims of "violent and abusive behaviour from some pupils".

They toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn. The 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea was forged by labourers from Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and south west England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford As they grafted to provide for their families back home hundreds lost their lives in landslides and accidents But one result of their sacrifice was "Manchester Docks", which was actually in Salford. Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

input.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
input.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
